## Description

Verify the `duration`, `easing` and `distance` options of the
object form of the `animation` prop of `Stack.Screen`. Pass: `duration` sets
how long both the push and the pop take and keeps a pop that is shorter than
its push shorter, `easing` changes the curve of a played transition (on Android
not of the predictive back gesture), `distance` sets how far `fadeFromBottom`
and `fadeFromTop` move, and an invalid value plays `default` instead.

## Note

- Wait for every transition to finish before the next tap.
- Static: the screen does not move and stays fully visible for the whole
  transition.
- **Known issue:** iOS: the back swipe plays UIKit's own pop, whatever the
  options (https://github.com/software-mansion/react-native-screens-labs/issues/2066).

## Steps

### Baseline

1. Launch the app and navigate to the **Stack Animation Preset Options** screen
   (on Android, launch the screen directly, see Setup).

   - [ ] "Home" is yellow with a dark frame at the screen edge and the title
         "Home".
   - [ ] No header is visible.
   - [ ] "next push" and "this screen" both read `slideFromRight`.
   - [ ] "next push header hidden" reads `true`.
   - [ ] "Push Blue" and "Push Red" are the only buttons.

---

### Duration

1. Set "next push" to `slideFromRight 2000 ms`, then tap "Push Blue".

   - [ ] "Blue" travels in from the right while "Home" travels out to the
         left, together, over about 2 seconds, five times as long as a plain
         `slideFromRight`. The motion speeds up at the start and
         slows down at the end.

2. On "Blue", set "this screen" to `slideFromRight 100 ms`, then tap "Pop".

   - [ ] The pop is over almost at once: "Home" is shown in about a tenth of a
         second.

3. On "Home", set "next push" to `fadeFromBottom 2000 ms`, then tap
   "Push Blue".

   - [ ] "Blue" rises a short distance, about a twelfth of the height, while
         fading in, and settles over about 2 seconds, slowing down strongly
         at the end. "Home" is static (see Note).

4. On "Blue", tap "Pop".

   - [ ] "Blue" sinks the same short distance while fading out, in clearly
         less time than the push took. "Home" is static.

---

### Easing

1. On "Home", set "next push" to `slideFromRight 2000 ms linear`, then tap
   "Push Blue".

   - [ ] Both screens move at one constant speed for the whole 2 seconds,
         with no speeding up at the start and no slowing down at the end.

2. On "Blue", tap "Pop". On "Home", set "next push" to
   `slideFromRight 2000 ms overshoot`, then tap "Push Blue".

   - [ ] "Blue" travels most of the way in quickly, then passes its resting
         position by about a tenth of the width: its left frame edge leaves
         the screen and a strip of the background shows at the right edge.
   - [ ] "Blue" then slowly settles back to rest.

---

### Distance

1. On "Blue", tap "Pop". On "Home", set "next push" to
   `fadeFromBottom 2000 ms 50%`, then tap "Push Blue".

   - [ ] "Blue" rises a long way while fading in: it starts about half the
         screen height lower, far below where it started in Duration step 3, and
         slows down into place. "Home" is static.

2. On "Blue", tap "Pop".

   - [ ] "Blue" sinks about half the screen height while fading out. "Home"
         is static.

3. On "Home", set "next push" to `fadeFromBottom 2000 ms 300`, then tap
   "Push Blue".

   - [ ] "Blue" rises a long way while fading in, about a third of the screen
         height on a phone and clearly further than in Duration step 3. Nothing
         slides in sideways and "Home" is static.

4. On "Blue", tap "Pop". On "Home", set "next push" to
   `fadeFromTop 2000 ms 50%`, then tap "Push Blue".

   - [ ] Mirrored vertically: "Blue" drops in from about half the screen
         height above while fading in. "Home" is static.

---

### Invalid values

1. On "Blue", tap "Pop". On "Home", set "next push" to
   `invalid: distance on slideFromRight`, then tap "Push Blue".

   - [ ] The `default` push plays instead.
   - [ ] Android: "Blue" slides in a short distance from the right while
         fading in, and "Home" slides the same distance to the left.
   - [ ] iOS: UIKit's push: "Blue" enters from the right, and "Home" moves
         about a third of the width to the left and dims.

2. On "Blue", set "this screen" to `fadeFromBottom 2000 ms 50%`, then to
   `invalid: bezier x1 = 1.5`, and tap "Pop".

   - [ ] The `default` pop plays instead: "Blue" does not sink.
   - [ ] Android: "Blue" slides a short distance to the right while fading
         out, and "Home" slides back in from the left.
   - [ ] iOS: UIKit's pop: "Blue" leaves to the right, and "Home" returns
         from the left.

## Steps - Android

### Predictive back gesture

1. On "Home", set "next push" to `slideFromRight 2000 ms overshoot`, tap
   "Push Blue", then swipe in slowly from the left screen edge to near the
   right edge and release.

   - [ ] While the finger moves, "Blue" follows it to the right and "Home" is
         revealed from the left at the same rate.
   - [ ] On release the pop completes from that position and only "Home" is
         shown.
   - [ ] "Home" never moves past its resting position, neither during the
         swipe nor after the release.

2. Tap "Push Blue", swipe in from the left screen edge to the middle, then
   swipe back to the edge and release.

   - [ ] "Blue" returns to rest with no residual offset.
   - [ ] "Home" is hidden again and nothing is popped.

## Steps - iOS

### Header back button

1. On "Home", set "next push" to `slideFromRight 100 ms` and "next push header
   hidden" to `false`, then tap "Push Blue".

   - [ ] "Blue" and the header with the title "Blue" appear within a blink.

2. On "Blue", set "next push" to `slideFromRight 2000 ms`, then tap
   "Push Red".

   - [ ] Both screens travel for about 2 seconds.
   - [ ] The header title crossfades from "Blue" to "Red" over the same 2
         seconds.

3. Tap the back button in the header.

   - [ ] The pop takes about 2 seconds.
   - [ ] The header shows "Blue" and a back button at the end, with nothing
         left over.

4. Tap the back button in the header.

   - [ ] "Home" is shown within a blink.
   - [ ] No header is visible and nothing of it is left over.

---

### Back swipe

1. Tap "Push Blue", then swipe in from the left screen edge and release past
   the middle.

   - [ ] "Blue" follows the finger and pops when released (see Note).
